content.rationale:
The dependent is a machine artifact - the partial policy carried as Quint state over the registry - so the gate is run over it rather than read: `specs/drafts/discard_partial_check.qnt` imports the record form, its two states and the registry variable from `draft_state` (tvtnokzu, `specs/drafts/state.qnt`), imports one action, the act state and the three act values from the model at `specs/drafts/discard_partial.qnt`, and fixes the interface that model must carry: module `draft_discard_partial`, the type `Act = Change | Forget | Remove`, the variable `acts: str -> Set[Act]` (the per-draft act state), and one action `discardPartial(handles: List[str], completed: str -> Set[Act], failed: bool)` over `records` and `acts`, total over its three inputs. `completed` maps a named handle to the acts this attempt completes beyond the ones already completed; `failed` says whether the attempt failed before the commit. The model imports the registry from `./state` and the commit action from `./discard_commit` (nytszsml, `specs/drafts/discard_commit.qnt`), so the commit itself stays that model's. The check imports only the interface and reads no helper, and the model must not define the check's own `gate`-prefixed helpers (`gateAll`, `gateNamed`, `gateActsOf`, `gateCompleted`, `gateAfterActs`, `gateRest`, `gateAccepted`, `gateWithoutNamed`, `gateCommitReady`), because the TLA+ flattener merges the two modules' definitions and a shared name would shadow the check's condition; an initializer named `init` is likewise not the model's to define, since `draft_state` already exports that name.

The check seeds a registry the prerequisites admit: three open drafts (`h1`, `h2`, `h3`) over two nodes and two landed records (`h4`, `h5`), each filed under its own handle through the state module's own constructors, with no act completed. It records the registry and the act state immediately before each step, together with the call's three inputs, and then runs the model's action, so every invariant relates the state after a step both to the state before it and to the inputs that step was given. A call pool covers an empty call; a failure after one act, after two and after all three; non-failing attempts completing one act and two; a commit in one call; a two-draft failure with one draft fully cleared and the other part-way; a two-draft commit; a two-draft call with one draft incomplete; a two-draft failure after every act; a landed record prepared; an open record mixed with a landed one; and an open record mixed with a handle the registry does not hold. A separate `retry` step is enabled in every state whose named record is open: it completes every act still to be done and fails nothing, so the checker reaches it from every reachable partial act state.

The invariants pin the policy from the three sides its prerequisites fix. `ActsOnlyGrow`, `ActsGrowByCall`, `UnnamedActsUntouched` and `FailureKeepsCompletedActs` - a handle's act state after a step is exactly the one before it plus the acts this attempt completed, never less, so a failure rolls no completed act back; a handle the call does not name keeps its act state and no handle gains one. `FailureLeavesRegistry` and `FailureLeavesNamedOpen` - a failed attempt leaves the registry exactly as it stood and every named record at its handle, field for field, so an open draft is still open. `NoRemovalBeforeCommit` and `CommitIsExact` - a call reaches the commit exactly when nothing failed, every named handle's three acts are complete and every named handle is an open record, and such a call removes exactly the named records; any other call leaves the registry unchanged, so a call has those two outcomes and no third. `RetryCommits` and `RetryClearsActs` - the retry completes the three acts and removes exactly the named record, from every reachable partial act state. `OthersUntouched`, `LandedNeverRemoved`, `NoRecordAdded` and `WholeCallAtomic` carry the retention the commit model already fixes: a landed record is never removed or rewritten, no record the call does not name changes, no record is added, and the removal is one act of the whole call. Thirteen runs execute one case each and assert its outcome: a failure after the first act, after two, and after all three, each leaving the completed acts, the registry and the open record in place; a retry after a failure completing the remaining acts and reaching the commit; a retry act by act that does not commit until the last act; a retry over a draft every act of which a failed call already cleared, which completes nothing and still commits; a commit in one call; a failure leaving every unnamed record as it was; a landed record never touched; a two-draft failure followed by a retry that removes both named records; an empty call that completes no act and removes nothing; and a call naming an absent handle, which refuses whole.

Each prerequisite is used for one thing. qznqvpyr states the policy: the acts a failed discard completed stand, the named record remains and the draft stays open, and a re-run goes on through an already-cleared part to the commit - the acts-only-grow, failure-leaves-registry and retry invariants and runs read those clauses as observables, and the check demands no rule those clauses do not state. nytszsml fixes where the commit sits and what an accepted call removes; the model delegates the commit to that action, and `NoRemovalBeforeCommit`, `CommitIsExact` and the refusal runs keep the composite model from committing on a crafted path of its own. tvtnokzu fixes the record's form, its two states and the registry map; the check imports that module and restates none of it, so the record shape, the states and the base stay the state model's.

The check is run mechanically. `quint typecheck specs/drafts/discard_partial_check.qnt` checks the grammar and the types, including that the model exposes the named type, variable and action with the three-input signature. `quint verify specs/drafts/discard_partial_check.qnt --main=draft_discard_partial_check --init=initCheck --backend=tlc --invariant=NoRemovalBeforeCommit,CommitIsExact,FailureLeavesRegistry,FailureLeavesNamedOpen,FailureKeepsCompletedActs,ActsOnlyGrow,ActsGrowByCall,UnnamedActsUntouched,RetryCommits,RetryClearsActs,OthersUntouched,LandedNeverRemoved,NoRecordAdded,WholeCallAtomic --max-steps=6` runs the explicit-state checker over every trace to the bound. `quint test specs/drafts/discard_partial_check.qnt` executes the eleven runs. The module starts from its seeded registry rather than from the state module's empty `init`, so the verifier is given `--init=initCheck`; TLC keeps the run free of the Apalache flattening step, and a JDK-backed `--backend=apalache` is the same check when a JDK is present.

The check tracks no wording of the decision. It fixes the action's contract - the act state only grows and grows by exactly the acts an attempt completed; a failed attempt leaves the registry untouched; and a call that completes every named act without failing removes exactly the named open records, from any partial act state - which is what the decision models, so a rewording that leaves that contract unchanged leaves the check intact. It demands nothing beyond that contract: the order of the three acts among themselves, the jj invocations behind them, the refusal's wording, stream and exit status, the registry write's mechanism and the record's serialization are outside the model and outside the check, and the change abandonment, workspace forget and directory removal a real discard performs are not executed here. The seeded handles, node ids, edits, workspaces, bases and act sets are values the check chooses, none of them derived from a prerequisite. Until the model exists the check has nothing to run - the import of `./discard_partial` fails - so the policy is unenforced on the artifact's side. The node states no verdict: whether a particular artifact satisfies the check is a finding about a run, not content of this evaluation.
